From dependence to value

Source: vignettes/dependence-to-value.Rmd
dependence-to-value.Rmd
library(pollinatoR)

From a ratio to a dollar figure

A dependence ratio says what share of a crop’s yield is owed to pollinators. Multiplied by the crop’s production and price, it gives the value of that pollination: the dependence-ratio method of Gallai et al. (2009). This vignette takes a fitted estimand through to such a value, with an interval. The value is computed for each draw of the estimand, and the interval comes from the value draws.

Each printed value lists the estimand and its basis, the population, the price year, the currency and the source of the market inputs.

A simulated trial

The trial has three arms in twelve blocks: plants bagged against insects, plants left open, and plants pollinated by hand. The blocks lie in canola fields at three distances from native vegetation, four blocks per distance band. Open plants yield less the further the field is from vegetation; bagged and hand-pollinated plants do not depend on distance. The response is seed yield per plant in grams.

set.seed(2025)
n_block <- 12L
n_plant <- 6L
blocks <- sprintf("B%02d", seq_len(n_block))
bands <- c("0-100 m", "100-300 m", "over 300 m")
band <- setNames(rep(bands, each = 4L), blocks)
trial <- expand.grid(
  plant = seq_len(n_plant),
  trt = c("Bagged", "Open", "Hand"),
  block = blocks,
  stringsAsFactors = FALSE
)
trial$band <- band[trial$block]
block_effect <- setNames(rnorm(n_block, 0, 0.1), blocks)
open_mean <- setNames(c(2.4, 2.1, 1.8), bands)
arm_mean <- ifelse(
  trial$trt == "Bagged",
  1.4,
  ifelse(trial$trt == "Hand", 2.6, open_mean[trial$band])
)
mu <- arm_mean * exp(block_effect[trial$block])
trial$yield <- rgamma(nrow(trial), shape = 25, rate = 25 / mu)

pd <- pollin_data(trial, response = "yield", treatment = "trt", unit = "block")
ds <- pollin_design(
  pd,
  arms = c(excluded = "Bagged", open = "Open", supplemented = "Hand"),
  layout = "rcbd"
)

A population of distance bands

The trial’s blocks are not a sample of the district’s canola. Suppose a land use map shows 300 ha of canola within 100 m of native vegetation, 500 ha at 100 to 300 m and 1,200 ha beyond. pollin_population() declares the bands as strata weighted by those areas.

district <- pollin_population(
  "band",
  c("0-100 m" = 300, "100-300 m" = 500, "over 300 m" = 1200),
  label = "district canola, by distance to vegetation"
)
district
#> <pollin_population>
#>   label   : district canola, by distance to vegetation 
#>   strata  : 3 levels of band 
#>   weights : 0-100 m 0.15, 100-300 m 0.25, over 300 m 0.60 (area, normalised)

The estimand takes the population, and fitting with the bands as by gives each band its own treatment effect.

dep <- pollin_estimand(ds, "dependence", "ratio", "loss", population = district)
fit_dep <- pollin_fit(dep, by = "band")

Draws of the estimand

pollin_draws() draws the fixed effects from their sampling distribution and recomputes the expected yield in each arm for every draw. The loss share is formed from each pair of arm means. A further column holds the population: the area-weighted arm means, and the loss share formed from them.

dr_dep <- pollin_draws(fit_dep, n = 1000L, seed = 1L)
dr_dep
#> <pollin_draws>
#>   family   : dependence (E2) 
#>   scale    : ratio 
#>   basis    : loss 
#>   estimate : 1 - Bagged/Open (loss share) 
#>   response : yield 
#>   method   : simulation of the fixed effects 
#>   engine   : glmmTMB 
#>   draws    : 1000 
#>   columns  : 0-100 m, 100-300 m, over 300 m, population 
#>   note     : simulation draws cover fixed-effect uncertainty only
summary(dr_dep)[, c("level", "median", "conf.low", "conf.high")]
#>        level    median   conf.low conf.high
#> 1    0-100 m 0.4066923 0.33474198 0.4681777
#> 2  100-300 m 0.3338761 0.24476716 0.4011106
#> 3 over 300 m 0.1691020 0.07298917 0.2519253
#> 4 population 0.2613885 0.20722735 0.3106252

The planted loss shares are 0.42, 0.33 and 0.22 in the three bands. The population loss share is a ratio of population means, 1−∑wlow/∑whigh1 - \sum w\,\mathrm{low} / \sum w\,\mathrm{high}, and so weights each band by its area and its open yield.

Market inputs

pollin_market() records current production and its price. Current production means the crop as it is pollinated now, the open arm in the trial’s terms. The figures below are illustrative.

canola <- pollin_market(
  quantity = 3600,
  price = 700,
  unit = "t",
  currency = "AUD",
  year = 2025,
  source = "Illustrative inputs",
  crop = "canola"
)
canola
#> <pollin_market>
#>   crop     : canola 
#>   quantity : 3,600 t 
#>   price    : 700 AUD per t 
#>   year     : 2025 
#>   source   : Illustrative inputs

The dependence channel

pollin_value() needs a channel; there is no default. The dependence channel values the production that would be lost if pollinators were wholly excluded.

val_dep <- pollin_value(dr_dep, canola, channel = "dependence")
val_dep
#> <pollin_value>
#>   channel    : dependence - value lost under total exclusion of pollinators 
#>   value      : 658,700 AUD (95% interval 522,200 to 782,800) 
#>   basis      : 1 - Bagged/Open (loss share)
#>   level      : population 
#>   population : district canola, by distance to vegetation: 3 strata of band, weighted by area 
#>   price year : 2025 
#>   currency   : AUD 
#>   market     : 3,600 t at 700 AUD per t 
#>   source     : Illustrative inputs 
#>   attribution: agent all, product yield, crop canola 
#>   method     : simulation of the fixed effects (1000 draws) 
#>   assumptions:
#>     - No price response: the price is held fixed whatever the change in production.
#>     - Total-loss counterfactual: the value is the production lost if pollinators were wholly excluded, with no substitution by other pollinators or inputs.
#>     - The estimand draws are independent of the market draws.
#>     - The population is the strata of `band` (0-100 m 0.15, 100-300 m 0.25, over 300 m 0.60), weighted by area. Within each stratum the expected response under each arm comes from the fitted model and is taken to hold across the stratum's area; the population estimand is formed from the area-weighted arm means.

The value is computed per draw as D×P×QD \times P \times Q, with D=1−excluded/openD = 1 - \mathrm{excluded}/\mathrm{open}. Production without pollinators would be Q×excluded/openQ \times \mathrm{excluded}/\mathrm{open}, a loss of D×QD \times Q.

Price and production are rarely known exactly. They can be given as draws, one per estimand draw, matched by position.

set.seed(7)
canola_unc <- pollin_market(
  quantity = 3600,
  price = 700,
  unit = "t",
  currency = "AUD",
  year = 2025,
  source = "Illustrative inputs with uncertainty",
  quantity_draws = rlnorm(1000L, log(3600), 0.10),
  price_draws = rlnorm(1000L, log(700), 0.15),
  crop = "canola"
)
summary(pollin_value(dr_dep, canola_unc, channel = "dependence"))[
  , c("median", "conf.low", "conf.high", "currency")
]
#>     median conf.low conf.high currency
#> 1 657525.5 433818.4  989986.2      AUD

The median barely moves. The interval is wider because price and production are now uncertain too.

The deficit channel

The deficit channel values the yield lost because the crop’s pollination falls short of hand pollination: the gain if every plant were pollinated as well as by hand. It needs a supplemented arm, and a deficit estimand with basis = "gain".

def <- pollin_estimand(ds, "deficit", "ratio", "gain", population = district)
dr_def <- pollin_draws(pollin_fit(def, by = "band"), n = 1000L, seed = 1L)
pollin_value(dr_def, canola, channel = "deficit")
#> <pollin_value>
#>   channel    : deficit - value of closing the gap to hand pollination 
#>   value      : 835,500 AUD (95% interval 610,700 to 1,081,000) 
#>   basis      : Hand/Open - 1 (gain)
#>   level      : population 
#>   population : district canola, by distance to vegetation: 3 strata of band, weighted by area 
#>   price year : 2025 
#>   currency   : AUD 
#>   market     : 3,600 t at 700 AUD per t 
#>   source     : Illustrative inputs 
#>   attribution: agent all, product yield, crop canola 
#>   method     : simulation of the fixed effects (1000 draws) 
#>   assumptions:
#>     - No price response: the price is held fixed whatever the change in production.
#>     - Gap counterfactual: the value is the production gained if the whole crop received hand-supplemented pollination, at no change in costs.
#>     - The estimand draws are independent of the market draws.
#>     - The population is the strata of `band` (0-100 m 0.15, 100-300 m 0.25, over 300 m 0.60), weighted by area. Within each stratum the expected response under each arm comes from the fitted model and is taken to hold across the stratum's area; the population estimand is formed from the area-weighted arm means.

Here the value per draw is (hand/open−1)×P×Q(\mathrm{hand}/\mathrm{open} - 1) \times P \times Q, the gain over current production. In both channels the ratio is taken relative to the open arm, because QQ is open-pollinated production. That is why each channel accepts one ratio only: a loss share for dependence and a gain for deficit.

Why the dependence channel refuses a gain

The loss share DD and the gain g=open/excluded−1g = \mathrm{open}/\mathrm{excluded} - 1 come from the same two arm means, and g=D/(1−D)g = D/(1 - D). A gain multiplied by current production overstates the loss by the factor 1/(1−D)1/(1 - D), so the dependence channel refuses it.

dep_gain <- pollin_estimand(ds, "dependence", "ratio", "gain", population = district)
dr_gain <- pollin_draws(pollin_fit(dep_gain, by = "band"), n = 1000L, seed = 1L)
try(pollin_value(dr_gain, canola, channel = "dependence"))
#> Error : The `dependence` channel needs the share of current production lost without pollinators, D = 1 - low/high. A gain g = high/low - 1 relates to it as g = D / (1 - D), so valuing a gain overstates the loss by the factor 1/(1 - D). Refit the estimand with basis = "loss": `pollin_estimand(design, "dependence", "ratio", "loss")`.

A descriptive index from pollin_index() or a plain number is refused as well, because neither records the estimand it came from.

Sensitivity: two populations

The area weights are an input, and a different map gives a different value. To see how much, value the estimand under a second population and compare. Here a second population puts most of the canola close to vegetation.

near <- pollin_population(
  "band",
  c("0-100 m" = 1000, "100-300 m" = 600, "over 300 m" = 400),
  label = "canola mostly near vegetation"
)
dep_near <- pollin_estimand(ds, "dependence", "ratio", "loss", population = near)
dr_near <- pollin_draws(pollin_fit(dep_near, by = "band"), n = 1000L, seed = 1L)
rbind(
  summary(pollin_value(dr_dep, canola, channel = "dependence")),
  summary(pollin_value(dr_near, canola, channel = "dependence"))
)[, c("median", "conf.low", "conf.high", "currency")]
#>     median conf.low conf.high currency
#> 1 658699.0 522212.9  782775.6      AUD
#> 2 883006.5 763773.7 1003818.6      AUD

The first row is the district map, the second the map with most canola near vegetation. With production held at 3,600 t, the second value is higher, because the crop near vegetation loses a larger share without pollinators.

Adding values without counting twice

Values can be added only when they count different things. pollin_guard_doublecount() adds values draw by draw and stops when two of them overlap. It compares the pollinators each exclusion removed (agent, all of them here), the product valued and the crop.

The value of canola seed and the value of the oil pressed from it are not separate contributions: the oil’s value includes the seed’s. The guard refuses the sum.

oil <- pollin_market(
  quantity = 1500,
  price = 1600,
  unit = "t",
  currency = "AUD",
  year = 2025,
  source = "Illustrative inputs",
  crop = "canola"
)
try(pollin_guard_doublecount(
  seed = pollin_value(dr_dep, canola, channel = "dependence", product = "seed"),
  oil = pollin_value(dr_dep, oil, channel = "dependence", product = "oil")
))
#> Error : The values `seed` and `oil` are for two products ('seed' and 'oil') attributed to 'all' for the same crop (canola). The value of the processed product already contains the value of the raw one, so adding them counts it again; value one product.

Values for two crops, each from its own trial, do not overlap. A second small trial in faba bean gives a second value, and the guard adds the two.

set.seed(11)
faba_trial <- expand.grid(
  plant = seq_len(6L),
  trt = c("Bagged", "Open"),
  block = sprintf("F%d", seq_len(8L)),
  stringsAsFactors = FALSE
)
faba_mu <- ifelse(faba_trial$trt == "Open", 30, 24)
faba_trial$yield <- rgamma(nrow(faba_trial), shape = 20, rate = 20 / faba_mu)
faba_ds <- pollin_design(
  pollin_data(faba_trial, "yield", "trt", unit = "block"),
  c(excluded = "Bagged", open = "Open"),
  "rcbd"
)
faba_dr <- pollin_draws(
  pollin_fit(pollin_estimand(faba_ds, "dependence", "ratio", "loss")),
  n = 1000L,
  seed = 2L
)
faba <- pollin_market(
  quantity = 900,
  price = 450,
  unit = "t",
  currency = "AUD",
  year = 2025,
  source = "Illustrative inputs",
  crop = "faba bean"
)
pollin_guard_doublecount(
  canola = pollin_value(dr_dep, canola, channel = "dependence", product = "seed"),
  faba = pollin_value(faba_dr, faba, channel = "dependence", product = "seed")
)
#> <pollin_value_total>  sum of 2 values 
#>   total      : 729,800 AUD (95% interval 596,000 to 854,000) 
#>   price year : 2025 
#>   draws      : 1000 (added draw by draw, paired by index)
#>   components :
#>     - canola: 658,700 AUD; dependence; agent all, product seed, crop canola; source: Illustrative inputs
#>     - faba: 72,410 AUD; dependence; agent all, product seed, crop faba bean; source: Illustrative inputs

What the value assumes

Each printed value lists its assumptions:

  • No price response. The price is held fixed, although losing a large share of a crop’s production would raise its price.
  • A total-loss counterfactual, for the dependence channel. The value is the production lost if every pollinator were removed, with nothing in their place. It is not the loss from a partial decline.
  • Independence of the estimand and the market draws. A season that is poor for pollination may also be a season of high prices; the draws are paired as if the two were unrelated.

Within each stratum of a population, the trial’s expected yields are taken to hold across the stratum’s area, and the areas are taken as exact.

The value is gross: the revenue from the production at stake, before any costs. With the default simulation draws the interval covers the uncertainty in the fixed effects only, not the variation between blocks; pollin_draws() with method = "bootstrap" includes it, at the cost of refitting the model.

References

Gallai, N., Salles, J.-M., Settele, J., & Vaissière, B. E. (2009). Economic valuation of the vulnerability of world agriculture confronted with pollinator decline. Ecological Economics, 68(3), 810–821. https://doi.org/10.1016/j.ecolecon.2008.06.014
